RateLimitDecision {\n53\t    /// Whether dispatch is allowed.\n54\t    pub fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {\n55\t        matches!(self, RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n56\t    }\n57\t}\n58\t\n59\timpl std::fmt::Display for RateLimitDecision {\n60\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n61\t        match self {\n62\t            RateLimitDecision::Allowed => RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n73\t                model,\n74\t                current,\n75\t                limit,\n76\t            } => write!(\n77\t                f,\n78\t                \"model '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n79\t                model, current, limit\n80\t            ),\n81\t            RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n82\t                provider,\n83\t                requests_per_minute,\n84\t            } => write!(\n85\t                f,\n86\t                \"provider '{}' RPM limit exceeded ({}/min)\",\n87\t                provider, requests_per_minute\n88\t            ),\n89\t        }\n90\t    }\n91\t}\n92\t\n93\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n94\t// Token Bucket (file-based)\n95\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n96\t\n97\t/// On-disk token bucket state for RPM limiting.\n98\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n99\tpub struct TokenBucket {\n100\t    /// Current available tokens (fractional for smooth refill).\n101\t    pub tokens: f64,\n102\t    /// Maximum tokens (= requests_per_minute).\n103\t    pub capacity: u32,\n104\t    /// Last time tokens were refilled.\n105\t    pub last_refill: DateTime<Utc>,\n106\t}\n107\t\n108\timpl TokenBucket {\n109\t    pub(crate) fn new(capacity: u32) -> Self {\n110\t        TokenBucket {\n111\t            tokens: capacity as f64,\n112\t            capacity,\n113\t            last_refill: Utc::now(),\n114\t        }\n115\t    }\n116\t\n117\t    /// Refill tokens based on elapsed time since last refill.\n118\t    fn refill(&mut self) {\n119\t        let now = Utc::now();\n120\t        let elapsed_secs = (now - self.last_refill).num_milliseconds().max(0) as f64 / 1000.0;\n121\t        let refill_rate = self.capacity as f64 / 60.0; // tokens per second\n122\t        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed_secs * refill_rate).min(self.capacity as f64);\n123\t        self.last_refill = now;\n124\t    }\n125\t\n126\t    /// Try to consume one token. Returns true if successful.\n127\t    fn try_consume(&mut self) -> bool {\n128\t        self.refill();\n129\t        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {\n130\t            self.tokens -= 1.0;\n131\t            true\n132\t        } else {\n133\t            false\n134\t        }\n135\t    }\n136\t}\n137\t\n138\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n139\t// RateLimiter\n140\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n141\t\n142\t/// Enforces provider/model concurrency limits and RPM rate limiting.\n143\tpub struct RateLimiter {\n144\t    config: LimitsConfig,\n145\t    /// Directory for token bucket state files (`~/.needle/state/rate_limits/`).\n146\t    state_dir: PathBuf,\n147\t}\n148\t\n149\timpl RateLimiter {\n150\t    /// Create a rate limiter with the given config and state directory.\n151\t    pub fn new(config: LimitsConfig, state_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n152\t        RateLimiter {\n153\t `Allowed` if dispatch can proceed, or a specific reason why not.\n161\t    /// The caller should back off and retry if not allowed.\n162\t    pub fn check(\n163\t        &self,\n164\t        provider: Option<&str>,\n165\t        model: Option<&str>,\n166\t        registry: &Registry,\n167\t    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n168\t        // Check provider concurrency.\n169\t        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n170\t            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n171\t                if let Some(max_concurrent) = provider_limits.max_concurrent {\n172\t                    let decision =\n173\t                        self.check_provider_concurrency(provider_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n174\t                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n175\t                        return Ok(decision);\n176\t                    }\n177\t                }\n178\t            }\n179\t        }\n180\t\n181\t        // Check model concurrency.\n182\t        if let Some(model_name) = model {\n183\t            if let Some(model_limits) = self.config.models.get(model_name) {\n184\t                if let Some(max_concurrent) = model_limits.max_concurrent {\n185\t                    let decision =\n186\t                        self.check_model_concurrency(model_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n187\t                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n188\t                        return Ok(decision);\n189\t                    }\n190\t                }\n191\t            }\n192\t        }\n193\t\n194\t        // Check RPM.\n195\t        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n196\t            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n197\t                if let Some(rpm) = provider_limits.requests_per_minute {\n198\t                    let decision = self.check_rpm(provider_name, rpm)?;\n199\t                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n200\t                        return Ok(decision);\n201\t                    }\n202\t                }\n203\t            }\n204\t        }\n205\t\n206\t        Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n207\t    }\n208\t\n209\t    /// Check provider concurrency against the worker registry.\n210\t    fn check_provider_concurrency(\n211\t        &self,\n212\t        provider: &str,\n213\t        max_concurrent: u32,\n214\t        registry: &Registry,\n215\t    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n216\t        let workers = registry.list()?;\n217\t        let active_count = workers\n218\t            .iter()\n219\t            .filter(|w| w.provider.as_deref() == Some(provider))\n220\t            .count() as u32;\n221\t\n222\t        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n223\t            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n224\t                provider: provider.to_string(),\n225\t                current: active_count,\n226\t                limit: max_concurrent,\n227\t            })\n228\t        } else {\n229\t            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n230\t        }\n231\t    }\n232\t\n233\t    /// Check model concurrency against the worker registry.\n234\t    fn check_model_concurrency(\n235\t        &self,\n236\t        model: &str,\n237\t        max_concurrent: u32,\n238\t        registry: &Registry,\n239\t    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n240\t        let workers = registry.list()?;\n241\t        let active_count = workers\n242\t            .iter()\n243\t            .filter(|w| w.model.as_deref() == Some(model))\n244\t            .count() as u32;\n245\t\n246\t        if active_count >= bucket.\n258\t    fn check_rpm(&self, provider: &str, rpm: u32) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n259\t        if rpm == 0 {\n260\t            return Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed);\n261\t        }\n262\t\n263\t        let allowed = self.try_acquire_rpm_token(provider, rpm)?;\n264\t        if allowed {\n265\t            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n266\t        } else {\n267\t    /// Try to acquire an RPM token from the file-based token bucket.\n275\t    ///\n276\t    /// Uses flock for cross-process safety.\n277\t    fn try_acquire_rpm_token(&self, provider: &str, rpm: u32) -> Result<bool> {\n278\t        // Ensure the rate_limits directory exists.\n279\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.state_dir).with_context(|| {\n280\t            format!(\n281\t                \"failed to create rate_limits directory: {}\",\n282\t                self.state_dir.display()\n283\t            )\n284\t        })?;\n285\t\n286\t        let bucket_path = self.state_dir.join(format!(\"{provider}.json\"));\n287\t\n288\t        // Open or create the bucket file.\n289\t        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n290\t            .read(true)\n291\t            .write(true)\n292\t            .create(true)\n293\t            .truncate(false)\n294\t            .open(&bucket_path)\n295\t            .with_context(|| {\n296\t                format!(\n297\t                    \"failed to open rate limit bucket: {}\",\n298\t                    bucket_path.display()\n299\t                )\n300\t            })?;\n301\t\n302\t        // Exclusive lock for atomic read-modify-write.\n303\t        FileExt::lock_exclusive(&file).with_context(|| {\n304\t            format!(\n305\t                \"failed to acquire lock on rate limit bucket: {}\",\n306\t                bucket_path.display()\n307\t            )\n308\t        })?;\n309\t\n310\t        // Read current state.\n311\t        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&bucket_path).unwrap_or_default();\n312\t        let mut bucket: TokenBucket = if content.trim().is_empty() {\n313\t            TokenBucket::new(rpm)\n314\t        } else {\n315\t            serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap_or_else(|_| TokenBucket::new(rpm))\n316\t        };\n317\t\n318\t        // Update capacity if config changed.\n319\t        bucket.capacity = rpm;\n320\t\n321\t        // Try to consume a token.\n322\t        let allowed = bucket.try_consume();\n323\t\n324\t        // Write updated state.\n325\t        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&bucket)\n326\t            .context(\"failed to serialize token bucket state\")?;\n327\t        std::fs::write(&bucket_path, &json).with_context(|| {\n328\t            format!(\n329\t                \"failed to write rate limit bucket: {}\",\n330\t                bucket_path.display()\n331\t            )\n332\t        })?;\n333\t\n334\t        // Release lock.\n335\t        FileExt::unlock(&file).with_context(|| {\n336\t            format!(\n337\t                \"failed to release lock on rate limit bucket: {}\",\n338\t                bucket_path.display()\n339\t            )\n340\t        })?;\n341\t\n342\t        Ok(allowed)\n343\t    }\n344\t\n345\t    /// Check system resource health (CPU load and memory).\n346\t    ///\n347\t    /// Emits structured telemetry events when thresholds are exceeded; does not\n348\t    /// block dispatch. Logs tracing warnings in addition to telemetry for\n349\t    /// operator visibility.\n350\t    pub fn check_system_resources(\n351\t        cpu_load_warn: f64,\n352\t        memory_free_warn_mb: u64,\n353\t        telemetry: &Telemetry,\n354\t    ) {\n355\t        // CPU load: read /proc/loadavg on Linux.\n356\t        if let Ok(loadavg) = std::fs::read_to_string(\"/proc/loadavg\") {\n357\t            if let Some(load_str) = loadavg.split_whitespace().next() {\n358\t                if let Ok(load) = load_str.parse::<f64>() {\n359\t                    // Normalize by number of CPUs.\n360\t                    let num_cpus = std::thread::available_parallelism()\n361\t                        .map(|n| n.get())\n362\t                        .unwrap_or(1);\n363\t                    let normalized = load / num_cpus as f64;\n364\t                    if normalized > cpu_load_warn {\n365\t                        tracing::warn!(\n366\t                            load_1min = %load_str,\n367\t                            normalized = %format!(\"{:.2}\", normalized),\n368\t                            threshold = %format!(\"{:.2}\", cpu_load_warn),\n369\t                            \"CPU load exceeds warning threshold\"\n370\t                        );\n371\t                        // Emit structured telemetry event.\n372\t                        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated {\n373\t                            load_average: load,\n374\t                            threshold: cpu_load_warn,\n375\t                            core_count: num_cpus,\n376\t                        });\n377\t                    }\n378\t                }\n379\t            }\n380\t        }\n381\t\n382\t        // Memory: read /proc/meminfo on Linux.\n383\t        if let Ok(meminfo) = std::fs::read_to_string(\"/proc/meminfo\") {\n384\t            let mut mem_available_kb: Option<u64> = None;\n385\t            for line in meminfo.lines() {\n386\t                if line.starts_with(\"MemAvailable:\") {\n387\t                    if let Some(val) = line.split_whitespace().nth(1) {\n388\t                        mem_available_kb = val.parse().ok();\n389\t                    }\n390\t                    break;\n391\t                }\n392\t            }\n393\t            if let Some(avail_kb) = mem_available_kb {\n394\t                let avail_mb = avail_kb / 1024;\n395\t                if avail_mb < memory_free_warn_mb {\n396\t                    tracing::warn!(\n397\t                        available_mb = avail_mb,\n398\t                        threshold_mb = memory_free_warn_mb,\n399\t                        \"available memory below warning threshold\"\n400\t                    );\n401\t                    // Emit structured telemetry event.\n402\t                    let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::FleetMemoryLow {\n403\t                        free_mb: avail_mb,\n404\t                        threshold_mb: memory_free_warn_mb,\n405\t                    });\n406\t                }\n407\t            }\n408\t        }\n409\t    }\n410\t}\n411\t\n412\t// Provider/model concurrency limits and RPM rate limiting.\n//!\n//! Before dispatching an agent, the worker checks:\n//! 1. **Concurrency limits**: Are fewer than `max_concurrent` workers using\n//!    this provider/model? Checked via the worker registry.\n//! 2. **RPM limits**: Has the provider's requests-per-minute budget been\n//!    exceeded? Checked via a file-based token bucket.\n//!\n//! If either check fails, the caller should back off and retry.\n//!\n//! Depends on: `config`, `registry`, `types`.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse fs2::FileExt;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RateLimitDecision\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a rate limit check.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum RateLimitDecision {\n    /// Dispatch is allowed.\n    Allowed,\n    /// Provider concurrency limit reached.\n    ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n        provider: String,\n        current: u32,\n        limit: u32,\n    },\n    /// Model concurrency limit reached.\n    ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n        model: String,\n        current: u32,\n        limit: u32,\n    },\n    /// RPM limit reached for this provider.\n    RpmExceeded {\n        provider: String,\n        requests_per_minute: u32,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl RateLimitDecision {\n    /// Whether dispatch is allowed.\n    pub fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for RateLimitDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            RateLimitDecision::Allowed => write!(f, \"allowed\"),\n            RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n                provider,\n                current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n                provider, current, limit\n            ),\n            RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n                model,\n                current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"model '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n                model, current, limit\n            ),\n            RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n                provider,\n                requests_per_minute,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider '{}' RPM limit exceeded ({}/min)\",\n                provider, requests_per_minute\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Token Bucket (file-based)\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// On-disk token bucket state for RPM limiting.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct TokenBucket {\n    /// Current available tokens (fractional for smooth refill).\n    pub tokens: f64,\n    /// Maximum tokens (= requests_per_minute).\n    pub capacity: u32,\n    /// Last time tokens were refilled.\n    pub last_refill: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\nimpl TokenBucket {\n    pub(crate) fn new(capacity: u32) -> Self {\n        TokenBucket {\n            tokens: capacity as f64,\n            capacity,\n            last_refill: Utc::now(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Refill tokens based on elapsed time since last refill.\n    fn refill(&mut self) {\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        let elapsed_secs = (now - self.last_refill).num_milliseconds().max(0) as f64 / 1000.0;\n        let refill_rate = self.capacity as f64 / 60.0; // tokens per second\n        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed_secs * refill_rate).min(self.capacity as f64);\n        self.last_refill = now;\n    }\n\n    /// Try to consume one token. Returns true if successful.\n    fn try_consume(&mut self) -> bool {\n        self.refill();\n        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {\n            self.tokens -= 1.0;\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RateLimiter\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Enforces provider/model concurrency limits and RPM rate limiting.\npub struct RateLimiter {\n    config:    }\n\n    /// Check all rate limits before dispatching.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Allowed` if dispatch can proceed, or a specific reason why not.\n    /// The caller should back off and retry if not allowed.\n    pub fn check(\n        &self,\n        provider: Option<&str>,\n        model: Option<&str>,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        // Check provider concurrency.\n        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n                if let Some(max_concurrent) = provider_limits.max_concurrent {\n                    let decision =\n                        self.check_provider_concurrency(provider_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check model concurrency.\n        if let Some(model_name) = model {\n            if let Some(model_limits) = self.config.models.get(model_name) {\n                if let Some(max_concurrent) = model_limits.max_concurrent {\n                    let decision =\n                        self.check_model_concurrency(model_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check RPM.\n        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n                if let Some(rpm) = provider_limits.requests_per_minute {\n                    let decision = self.check_rpm(provider_name, rpm)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n    }\n\n    /// Check provider concurrency against the worker registry.\n    fn check_provider_concurrency(\n        &self,\n        provider: &str,\n        max_concurrent: u32,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        let workers = registry.list()?;\n        let active_count = workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| w.provider.as_deref() == Some(provider))\n            .count() as u32;\n\n        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n                provider: provider.to_string(),\n                current: active_count,\n                limit: max_concurrent,\n            })\n        } else {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check model concurrency against the worker registry.\n    fn check_model_concurrency(\n        &self,\n        model: &str,\n        max_concurrent: u32,\n        registry: &Registry,\n     .count() as u32;\n\n        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n                model: model.to_string(),\n                current: self.try_acquire_rpm_token(provider, rpm)?;\n        if allowed {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n        } else {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.state_dir).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to create rate_limits directory: {}\",\n                self.state_dir.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let bucket_path = self.state_dir.join(format!(\"{provider}.json\"));\n\n        // Open or create the bucket file.\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout {              duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id,    priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── FileSink ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Writes JSONL telemetry to `<log_dir>/<worker>-<session>.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Append-only, one line per event. The log directory is created if it\n/// does not exist.\npub struct FileSink {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    writer: std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n}\n\nimpl FileSink {\n    /// Construct a sink using the default log directory (`~/.needle/logs/`).\n    pub fn new(worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n        let log_dir = PathBuf::from(&home).join(\".needle\").join(\"logs\");\n        Self::with_dir(&log_dir, worker_id, session_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Construct a sink writing to a specific directory.\n    ///\n    /// Creates the directory (and parents) if it does not exist.\n    pub fn with_dir(log_dir: &Path, worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(log_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n        let filename = format!(\"{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl\");\n        let path = log_dir.join(filename);\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(FileSink {\n            path,\n            writer: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::io::BufWriter::new(file)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Return the path to the log file.\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file, bypassing the normal channel.\n    ///\n    /// This is called immediately after FileSink creation to ensure that even if\n    /// the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL file.\n    /// The event is written synchronously and flushed to disk.\n    fn write_boot_event_direct(\n        &self,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        Self::write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n            &self.writer,\n            &self.path,\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            version,\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), // 5 second timeout\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file with a timeout.\n    ///\n    /// This is a timeout-aware variant that prevents indefinite blocking on hung\n    /// filesystems (e.g., network filesystem issues, stale NFS mounts). If the\n    /// write takes longer than the timeout, it returns an error and the caller\n    /// can decide whether to continue or fail.\n    ///\n    /// The timeout is implemented by spawning a thread to do the blocking I/O\n    /// and joining with a timeout. If the timeout expires, the thread is detached\n    /// and will continue running (and eventually complete or be killed by the OS).\n    fn write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n        _writer: &std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n        path: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n        timeout: std::time::Duration,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::sync::mpsc;\n        use std::thread;\n\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: \"worker.booting\".to_string(),\n            worker_id: worker_id.to_string(),\n            session_id: session_id.to_string(),\n            sequence: 0,\n            bead_id: None,\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: None,\n            data: serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_id, \"version\": version }),\n            trace_id: None,\n            span_id: None,\n        };\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(&event)?;\n        let path_for_error = path.display().to_string();\n        let path_clone = path.to_path_buf();\n\n        // JoinHandle::join() has no timeout in Rust's std — use a channel with recv_timeout.\n        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Result<(), String>>();\n\n        // The JoinHandle is intentionally dropped on timeout: dropping detaches the thread,\n        // which continues running until it completes or the process exits.\n        let _handle = thread::spawn(move || {\n            let result: Result<(), String> = (|| {\n                let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                    .create(true)\n                    .append(true)\n                    .open(&path_clone)\n
